te.title: Stack SO2 creeping up
te.sit: Over the last hour the stack SO2 analyzer has crept from about 290 to about 440 ppm. Sulfur rate, strength and every bed inlet temperature are at their set points. The previous shift saw nothing unusual.

te.title: The air valves keep opening
te.sit: Converter at design rate. Over the week FV-101 and FV-102 have been opening further and the converter inlet pressure PI-200 is about 10 kPa above what it was after the turnaround.

te.title: Bed 1 is running hot
te.sit: Over the last half hour bed 1 exit has crept a few degrees above its usual 631 °C and the stack SO2 has doubled to above the 500 ppm permit. AIC-104 shows 12.0 % SO2, right on set point, and the sulfur rate has not changed.

te.title: The hot zone is moving down bed 1
te.sit: The middle thermocouple of bed 1 (TI-202) used to read close to the bed exit; this month it reads almost 20 °C lower. Bed 1 exit and the stack are normal.

te.title: White plume from the stack
te.sit: The field operator reports a dense white plume from the stack. AIT-307 (SO3 mist) and AIT-306 (SO2) are both higher than usual. The converter temperatures look normal.

te.title: Bed 2 inlet will not settle
te.sit: After TV-211 was repacked this morning, TIC-211 keeps swinging a degree or two around its set point and the bypass valve position jumps. The other loops are steady.

te.title: Two temperature loops at their limits
te.sit: TV-221 (bed 3 inlet) has closed fully and bed 3 inlet is above set point; TV-231 (bed 4 inlet) is wide open and bed 4 inlet is still below set point. Stack SO2 is rising.

te.title: Production falling although the sulfur valve opens
te.sit: FI-103 has fallen from 40.9 to about 32 t/h over the last half hour although FV-103 is now wide open. Air has followed the ratio. The sulfur tank level is normal.

te.title: Bed 3 is doing less work
te.sit: Bed 3 thermocouples read normal, yet the bed-4 temperature rise is larger than usual and the stack SO2 is up by a quarter. Nothing was changed.

te.title: Gas to the IPA is too hot
te.sit: TIC-251 has closed TV-251 fully but the gas to T-301 keeps rising; bed 5 inlet is also above its set point.

te.title: Bed 1 and bed 2 running cooler
te.sit: Over the last 40 minutes bed 1 exit has drifted from 631 to about 624 °C and bed 2 exit from 528 to about 523 °C. TIC-201 reads 420 °C on set point, the sulfur rate and SO2 strength are normal and the stack SO2 has hardly changed.

te.title: Second pass fading
te.sit: Since the start-up yesterday the stack SO2 has been near 500 ppm and bed 4 has a larger temperature rise than before the turnaround. Beds 1–3 look normal.

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Stack SO2 creeping up (SO3 Converter R-201)
meta.sit: Over the last hour the stack SO2 analyzer has crept from about 290 to about 440 ppm. Sulfur rate, strength and every bed inlet temperature are at their set points. The previous shift saw nothing unusual.

0.1.unit: R-201 is the five-bed SO₂ → SO₃ converter of a sulfur-burning sulfuric acid plant (125 t/h H₂SO₄, 100 % basis). K-101 blows 238.5 kNm³/h of dried air; 40.94 t/h of molten sulfur burns in F-101, B-101 raises steam, dilution air brings the gas to 12.0 % SO₂ / 9.0 % O₂ at 420 °C into bed 1. Beds 1–3 convert to 95.8 %; SH-201, E-201 and E-202 cool the gas between beds; the IPA T-301 absorbs SO₃; the return gas is reheated in E-202 and E-201 and goes to beds 4–5 (to 99.80 %), then E-205 and the final absorber T-302, and the stack (AIT-306, permit 500 ppm SO₂). Bed inlets are held by hot-gas bypass loops TIC-201…TIC-251.

rows.what: Stack SO₂ AIT-306 442 ppm (design 292 ppm); crept up over the last hour, flat for the last 35 min
Bed 4 temperature rise 22.1 °C (was 16.0 °C); TV-231 0.2 % and TV-241 0.1 % with TIC-231 428.9 °C and TIC-241 434.9 °C above set point
Sulfur 40.95 t/h, SO₂ strength 12.01 %, bed 1–3 inlets on set point; no alarm

0.4.ctx: Night shift at full rate, no maintenance or operating change reported, no alarm. One hour earlier (−01:00:00) the unit was on design: stack 292 ppm, bed-4 rise 16.0 °C, TV-231 38.9 %, TV-241 43.7 %.

R.1.p: Each bed is adiabatic: the gas heats up in proportion to the SO₂ it converts, until it nears equilibrium, which is lower the hotter the gas. The inlet temperature of each bed is held by a hot-gas bypass loop: more bypass gives a hotter inlet. Beds 1–3 make most of the SO₃; the IPA removes it, so beds 4–5 see a gas with ≈ 0.6 % SO₂ and almost no SO₃ and push the conversion to 99.8 %. Anything that sends more SO₂, or any SO₃, to bed 4 shows as a larger bed-4 rise and a higher stack SO₂; SO₃ that reaches bed 4 also pushes its equilibrium back.

R.2.eq: ΔT_bed ≈ 3.35 °C × ΔX (% points of conversion, 12 % SO₂ basis);   stack ppm ≈ 10⁶ · 0.12 · (1 − X) / 0.821

3.2.n: Bed-4 rise 22.1 °C against 16.0 °C: ΔX ≈ (22.1 − 16.0)/3.35 ≈ 1.82 % points more conversion in bed 4, so more SO₂ reaches bed 4 than the IPA return gas should carry. After the grab sample (T-5): bed-1 exit gas holds ≈ 4.60 % SO₂ and 7.87 % SO₃ (12 % SO₂, 9 % O₂, 63.1 % conversion). Mixing it into return gas of 0.61 % SO₂ / 69 ppm SO₃: SO₃ 4423 ppm ⇒ leak ≈ (4423 − 69)/(78700 − 69) = 5.5 %; SO₂ 0.82 % ⇒ (0.82 − 0.61)/(4.60 − 0.61) = 5.3 %. The two estimates agree: about 5.4 % of the return gas is bed-1 gas.

rows.c: Stack, mist and bed-4 rise all rose together: a real process change
Bed 2 inlet on set point but E-201 hot outlet 393 °C against 406 °C and TV-211 41.2 %: less gas or more heat loss on the E-201 hot side

3.5.tree:
TOP: stack SO₂ +150 ppm with beds 1–3 on design
 OR — more SO₂ / SO₃ reaching bed 4
    OR — bed-1 gas leaking into the return gas (E-201 / E-202 tubes)
    OR — feed gas through HV-112
    OR — gas bypassing bed 3
    OR — SO₃ slipping through the IPA
 OR — bed 4–5 catalyst converting less

3.5.cut: Single-element cut sets only: any one path gives the top event. The bed-4 rise (up, not down) removes the catalyst and analyzer branches.

3.10.n: None after the bed-balance discussion: all agree that bed 4 does more work, so more reactant reaches it.

5.7.n: The stack fell below 300 ppm 51 s after the repair, dipped to 257 ppm at 00:18:14, rose to 337 ppm at 00:26:52 while TV-241 reopened (from 00:25:08) and bed 5 cooled, and settled at 292 ppm by 00:40:00 with the bed-4 rise 15.2 °C. Verification sample at 00:37:25: SO₂ 0.61 %, SO₃ 69 ppm, the same as the model at design (0.60 %, 69.5 ppm: the normal IPA slip). The field message reports up to 200 ppm as the normal slip past the IPA, so 69 ppm is the baseline, not a remaining leak.

5.8.rule: If the stack SO₂ rises with beds 1–3 on design while the bed-4 rise grows and TV-231/TV-241 close, take a grab sample at the E-201 cold outlet: SO₃ there means bed-1 gas is leaking into the return gas.

6.3.fut: A leak between two gas streams in an acid plant does not raise an alarm by itself; the bed temperature rises are the cheapest leak detector. The model shows how far it can go: at a 6 % leak of the bed-1 gas the stack would reach 487 ppm, 13 ppm under the permit.

6.4.how: Assumed: without the repair a growing leak forces a 10 % rate cut for the 90 days to the turnaround: 0.10 × 9359 $/h (model margin) × 24 h × 90 d.

6.5.again:
Compute the temperature rise of every bed before believing an analyzer.
Use field checks that each kill one path, and send them together.
Estimate the leak from the gas sample with a mixing balance.
6.5.never:
Never blame the stack analyzer before checking that the process moved with it.
Never leave the bed 4–5 loops saturated without asking why.
